AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.
This DAR was filed on 10.03.2023 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties.
The DAR is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 13.11.2022 in which one Sh. Shubham Singh S/o Sh.Jagdamba Prasad Singh (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

As per petitioner, at the relevant date, at about 09.15 A.M, when he was returning back from Azamgarh,
U.P. via train and when he reached at Old Delhi Railway Station, he booked an auto TSR bearing registration no. DL-1RP-1343 to his rental accommodation in Moti Nagar, Delhi and upon reaching Tis Hazari Court, Gate No.1 suddenly a DTC Bus bearing registration number DL-1PC- 7271 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") whose driver was operating the vehicle recklessly and on the wrong side of the road, hit the TSR from front side.

It is further stated that after the accident,
he was taken to St. Stephen's Hospital where MLC PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:

It is further stated that due to this accident, he sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that due to this accident, he went through multiple surgeries and had spent around Rs.4,50,000/- and incurred Rs.2,93,849/- towards medicines.

It is further stated that due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle who was driving his vehicle in a very rash and negligent manner, this accident happened and he suffered the loss and sustained 20% permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb.

It is further stated that at the time of accident, he was 26 years of age and was preparing for UPSC and providing tuitions and working as a software developer and was earning Rs.40,000/- to Rs. 45,000/- per month from that vocation.

ISSUE NO.1 "Whether the petitioner Shubham suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 13.11.2022 at about 09.20 Hrs. involving vehicle bearing registration No.DL-1PC-7271 driven by the respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the respondents no. 2 and insured with the respondent No.3?OPP."

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his person on account of negligence and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

16 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
17. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

Date:
2024.11.07 12:39:25 +0530 pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment,
special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA Date: 2024.11.07 12:39:28 +0530
object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject Shubham (I) (Fir 438/2022/Civil Lines) vs Rajesh Kumar (Go Digit) on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157237178/
8 like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 19.

The petitioner has placed on judicial file the treatment records and original medical bills vide Ex.
PW-1/3(colly) and Ex.PW-1/4 (colly) respectively.

As per the said documents, PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.11.07 12:39:32 +0530 petitioner has incurred expenses to the tune of Rs.2,92,060.36/-.
In the absence of any contest to the said documents (placed on record by the petitioner), the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.2,92,060.36/- under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 20.

As per medical documents, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and also sustained 20%
permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb.

As per disability certificate no.1944 dated 12.04.2024 issued by Aruna Asaf Ali Govt. Hospital, Delhi, petitioner is a case of ''FUC Of PCL Injury Lt. Knee'' and was found to have sustained 20% permanent physical impairment in relation to left lower limb.

PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs. 50,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of income 21.

In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the petitioner claims that he was 26 years of age and was providing tuition and working as a software developer and was earning Rs.40,000/- to Rs. 45,000/- per Shubham (I) (Fir 438/2022/Civil Lines) vs Rajesh Kumar (Go Digit) on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157237178/
9 month.
He placed on record the ITRs for the assessment years 2022-23, 2023-24 & 2024-25 vide Ex. PW-1/6 (Colly).
Accordingly, for the purpose of computation of compensation amount, the ITR of the petitioner for the A.Y. 2022-2023 is considered.
As per ITR for the A.Y. 2022-23, the gross total income of the petitioner is Rs.4,95,000/- and same is considered for computation of compensation amount.
The medical records placed on record by petitioner reflect that the petitioner sustained a grievous injuries which resulted into 20% permanent physical disability with respect to left lower limb.
The above documents are sufficient to uphold the claim of the petitioner to the effect that he was unable to resume his vocation since the date of accident.

In PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.11.07 12:39:39 +0530 view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner has become unfit for work for about 06 months due to the injuries.

As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.2,47,500/-
(Rs.4,95,000/- X 6/12).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 22.
Petitioner claimed in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A that he has become permanently disabled after the accident and could not perform his work by resuming his duties.
Admittedly, petitioner has suffered 20% permanent physical impairment with respect to left lower limb and the said disability would definitely impede his capacity to work in the household.
Therefore, in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 10%.
This Tribunal has already assumed the annual income of petitioner to be Rs.4,95,000/- at the relevant time.

As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned, we may look into the photocopy of petitioner's Aadhar Card which is Ex. PW1/2, as per the said document, the date of birth of petitioner was 16.02.1996.
The date of accident is 13.11.2022.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident was around 26 years.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA Date: 2024.11.07 12:39:42 +0530 Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121,
which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '17' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed at the relevant time.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
17. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment,
special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA Date: 2024.11.07 12:39:28 +0530
object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject Shubham (I) (Fir 438/2022/Civil Lines) vs Rajesh Kumar (Go Digit) on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157237178/
8 like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
18.
Accordingly, the aforementioned disability certificate could be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Union of India in Writ Petition (s) (Civil ) No (s). 534/2020 date of order 16/11/2021.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
Therefore, in the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be assessed at 10%.
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA Date: 2024.11.07 12:39:42 +0530 Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121,
which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '17' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.
